title: Putting the FINAL Nail in the Coffin and Laying PED Fanboys to Rest for GO
summary: A 2h15 rebuttal of Revival Fitness's response on PEDs and morality. NH argues his anti-PED case rests on facts (health, sustainability, addiction, early death), not moral superiority, and dismantles pro-PED arguments such as 'Arnold-era guys are still alive', 'everyone dies anyway' and 'recreational doses are fine'. He also covers TRT and blood-test marketing to teens, why effective stigma backed by reasons works, and influencers' responsibility to their audience.
claims: NH says his first video argued that the PED debate is about facts and reason, not morality; it is PED users who retreat to morality because they lose on the facts
Naturals are not inherently better beings; what makes them 'better' is logical choices around health, accountability and sustainability
Naturals are superior in every way except the physical: the only pro-PED arguments are getting bigger, stronger and faster
Shame comes from within: critics only feel shamed because part of them knows PED use is damaging
'Shaming pushes people to drugs' is the same excuse as 'fat shaming makes me eat more' and shifts responsibility onto others
Rules backfire when they are empty morality with no reasons; the DARE/war-on-drugs approach failed because it gave no reasons, not because stigma itself fails
Giving people real reasons (addiction, psychosis, health costs) works better than blind stigma, and abandoning anti-drug messaging altogether has made drug use worse
Staying neutral on PEDs effectively sides with them, because pro-PED messaging is everywhere on YouTube fitness
PED prevalence came from cultural influence on YouTube fitness, so it can be reduced by preaching against it
Nobody is objective; objectivity is subjectivity enough people agree on
Almost every lifter starts out of insecurity, and Larry Wheels said he started PEDs out of insecurity after seeing others take them
Almost none of the young men fantasizing about PEDs will make it as pros, models or actors; those at the top were exceptional before drugs, and many pros started at 14-15 before puberty ended
Failed PED users don't just lose money; every cycle adds damage to their health
99.9% of PED users get nowhere, and trading years of life for no payoff is a bad trade
Nobody can compete in pro bodybuilding without drugs, which is exactly why PEDs are so tempting
NH is straight edge against inebriation but drinks a glass of wine roughly every two months; his issue is dependence, and PED users physically cannot live without the drug
Whataboutism (alcohol is also bad, murder is worse) does not make PEDs less bad
Coming off or lowering doses doesn't prove PED users aren't addicted; pros usually come off because doctors tell them they will die otherwise, and 'downsizing' trends hide health problems
Most people start PEDs uneducated and are blindsided by side effects; where stigma is low (Brazil, South Korea, India), there is even less knowledge
Young men think they are invincible, which is why men die more from drug abuse than women
PED use 'chases the dragon': tolerance and stagnating gains lead users to take more
John Meadows died at 49 on heavy use; if heavy use kills men in their 50s, mild use is not 'okay'
NH liked Rich Piana because he was honest about his use, called out liars and admitted he would die young
NH watches and respects some enhanced creators like Jujimufu and John Meadows; he doesn't lump all PED users together but says they are all damaging their health
NH claims to be a better role model for naturals than Ronnie Coleman, CBum or Jujimufu, while admitting they beat him on motivation, physique, charisma and entertainment
Real confidence and pride come from building a body without exogenous hormones; PEDs take that away
'Arnold-era guys are still alive' is survivorship bias: they are only in their late 60s-70s, while the average obese American lives to about 80, and the many who died are unknown
The Pumping Iron follow-up documentary found that many of the gym regulars around Arnold had died, were ill, or were broke and still chasing the dream
Arnold had several open-heart surgeries and his wealth gives him medical access that ordinary PED users won't have
Individual tolerance varies: one resilient drug user surviving (like Joey Diaz) doesn't make the drug safe
Healthy people rarely die in their 60s; some natural lifters born in the 1920s-30s lived into their 90s and beyond
'You might die tomorrow anyway' is no way to plan a life; because we don't know when we'll die, we should control what we can
Time is the most valuable resource; even three years of life lost is a tragedy
NH has sat in hospitals with people who said they'd never regret living fast; they all did
PED users lose on both ends: worse quality of life from side effects and shorter life
PED side effects can be permanent, unlike a bad job or a bad relationship
Blood work is useless for naturals; teens who get low-T results will seek out providers who prescribe TRT, so promoting hormone tests to a young audience is irresponsible
The therapeutic fallacy: TRT is presented as healthy because some people need it, but true hypogonadism among teens is around 0.2% or less
Prescription testosterone has the same side effects as underground testosterone at the same dose; clinical sourcing adds safety but not immunity
Steroids are even more damaging for women, whose side effects persist after the anabolic effects fade
Stigma exists for a reason; if it doesn't work, revamp it rather than drop it, the way you revise speeding laws
Enhanced YouTubers never came clean voluntarily; they were exposed, and they lied with 'just TRT', 'downsizing' and 'reached my natural limit'
Influencers are responsible for how their content affects their audience; many young viewers are warming up to PEDs through 'neutral' content
NH has talked friends out of PEDs and lost others he couldn't help
